newsitem.title: UK: Russia seeks less aluminium raw material imports.
newsitem.headline: Russia seeks less aluminium raw material imports.

text.p: The Russian aluminium industry will be greatly strengthened and much less reliant on overseas suppliers if aluminium producers invest in maintaining the domestic raw material base, metals analysts Roskill said.
In a press release on its new report on Bauxite and Alumina in the CIS it said that the CIS produces 16 percent of the world's total aluminium output.
But in 1995 Russia imported over 20 percent of its aluminium material from outside the CIS, while 28 percent of CIS alumina was produced from imported bauxite.
But the pattern is changing and domestic material is starting to increase its share, Roskill said.

The report said there is a major need to rebuild old bauxite and alumina production plants as production costs will only be reduced by large scale modernisation programmes, but funds are insufficient.

It said the most expedient solution would be to form financial-industrial groups incorporating organisations from all stages of the production chain - from bauxite mining to primary aluminium and/or rolled material producers.
The formation of such a group would enable members to avoid VAT and special taxes when transferring output to the next ornagisation in the production chain.
Roskill said this would be equivalent to an increase in working capital of over 20 percent and would reduce production costs of the end-product.
In addition, the participation of electricity suppliers and rail companies in the financial-industrial group would reduce energy and transportation costs and therefore production costs.
